name: Randall Glein
current_role: Co-founder & Partner, DFJ Growth; independent director, SpaceX (since Feb 2026)
profile: Randy Glein co-founded growth-stage VC firm DFJ Growth (joined 2002), investing in AI, space, deeptech and defense tech. A long-time SpaceX backer, he was a board observer from 2009 before joining SpaceX's board as an independent director in 2026; earlier he was CFO of FeedBurner (acquired by Google) and an executive at DIRECTV.
interesting_fact: He sat in on SpaceX board meetings as an observer for roughly 16 years (from 2009) before becoming a formal independent director ahead of SpaceX's IPO, with an expected seat on the audit committee.
deep_cut_fact: Before investing in rockets he built satellites' links himself: he began as a satellite communications engineer at GM Hughes Electronics and helped launch DIRECTV; he holds an EE degree from Univ. of Florida, an MS EE from USC Viterbi (1990) and a UCLA MBA, and is a near-scratch golfer.
notes: No personal contact published. Best route is via DFJ Growth (dfjgrowth.com; site blocks scripted access) or SpaceX media relations. Low public profile.

name: John M. Evans
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and director, Beam Therapeutics (since 2017)
profile: John Evans has led Beam Therapeutics, the Cambridge, MA base-editing gene-therapy company, since 2017, joining from ARCH Venture Partners as its launch CEO. Before that he was an early employee and SVP of corporate development and portfolio leadership at Agios, where he helped bring IDH inhibitors IDHIFA and TIBSOVO forward and co-led the Celgene alliance.
interesting_fact: Under Evans, Beam reported what it called the first-ever clinical genetic correction of a disease-causing mutation, with its in-vivo base editor BEAM-302 for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (2025).
deep_cut_fact: A gene-editing CEO with a humanities start: he earned a bachelor's in English with distinction from Yale before adding a Penn biotechnology master's and Wharton MBA; early career stops included MedImmune, McKinsey's pharma practice and Infinity Pharmaceuticals.
notes: Has said on podcasts 'I do not come from this field' — comfortable discussing the business side of biotech. Route via 1AB media contact.

name: Bill Wilson
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Townsquare Media (NYSE: TSQ)
profile: Bill Wilson joined Townsquare Media in 2010 and rose from Chief Content & Digital Officer to co-CEO and then CEO, steering the local-radio owner into a 'digital-first' local media and marketing company. He previously spent nine years at AOL, ending as President of AOL Media, and began his career in the record business at Arista/BMG.
interesting_fact: Radio Ink named him its Radio Executive of the Year for 2021; he describes Townsquare's strategy as using 'radio as a Trojan horse to build a digital-first company.'
deep_cut_fact: He started as a product manager at Arista Records working on artists from the Notorious B.I.G. and Kenny G to Sarah McLachlan and Spiritualized, and later won a 2006 Emmy Award for AOL's Live 8 program; he graduated summa cum laude in economics from SUNY Stony Brook.
notes: Gives frequent trade-press interviews (Barrett Media, Radio Ink, Boyar Research Substack) — receptive to media; route via IR/Townsquare press office.

name: David S Wichmann
current_role: Independent director, Boston Scientific (since 2021) and Privia Health Group (since 2023); former CEO, UnitedHealth Group
profile: David Wichmann spent over two decades at UnitedHealth Group, rising from SVP of corporate development (1998) to CFO, president and then CEO from 2017 until early 2021, when Optum chief Andrew Witty succeeded him. He now serves as an independent director of medtech maker Boston Scientific and physician-enablement company Privia Health.
interesting_fact: He ran the largest US health insurer/health-services group as CEO (2017–2021) after earlier serving as its CFO and president — an accountant-turned-CEO of one of America's biggest companies by revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he was an auditor: an Illinois State University accounting graduate who made partner at Arthur Andersen, then moved to UnitedHealth in 1998 as SVP of corporate development.
notes: Low public profile since leaving UnitedHealth; no personal channels found. Approach only via board-company corporate secretary/press offices (Boston Scientific, Privia).

name: Brian Raduenz
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, AEVEX Aerospace (NYSE: AVEX); director, Karman Holdings; director nominee, Lyntris
profile: Brian Raduenz is a retired US Air Force lieutenant colonel who built AEVEX Aerospace, a defense-tech/drone and ISR company, from Merlin Global Services, serving as CEO 2014–Nov 2025 through multiple acquisitions before becoming executive chairman. He also sits on the boards of space/defense supplier Karman Holdings and defense connectivity company Lyntris.
interesting_fact: In the Air Force he oversaw early operational use of remotely piloted aircraft and spent his final decade leading government oversight of MQ-1 Predator and MQ-9 Reaper production and sustainment — then built a public drone/defense-tech company.
deep_cut_fact: An Air Force Academy electrical-engineering graduate (plus an AFIT MS EE), he was once named Air Force Outstanding Senior Engineer of the Year and served as Director of White House Presidential Contingency Programs under President George W. Bush.
notes: Bio sourced from Lyntris S-1/A (SEC). AEVEX site blocked scripted access; route via AEVEX Aerospace corporate communications. Web-search budget was exhausted during this lane, so contact lookup was limited.
